text:
Rina: Small UX follow-up from the dashboard chairs review: modal stack order is inconsistent. When launching a settings modal from inside an inline drawer the drawer backdrop remains above the modal. Not great.

Omar: Repro: open project -> click 'Manage keys' (drawer) -> from drawer click 'Revoke key' -> confirm modal appears but drawer backdrop sits on top.

Tess: I think it's because drawer uses --z-drawer: 9000 and modal default is --z-modal: 8500. Should be the other way around for nested flows.

Rina: Suggest we add nesting rules: child overlays should always have z-index higher than their parent. Could be implemented by tracking overlay-depth in the overlay manager and applying --z-base + depth*10.

DesignQAbot: Recommendation: overlay manager depth approach reduces ad-hoc z rules. Also run cross-browser checks for stacking contexts (transform, opacity).

Omar: I'll prototype overlay-depth. If we use --z-base: 8000 then drawer depth 1 -> 8010, modal inside drawer -> 8020.

Tess: Also noticed toast placement during drawer flows lands center-bottom which collides with drawer actions. Can we hide toasts while drawer is open or temporarily move them?

Rina: Hiding toasts seems risky. Maybe the overlay manager can emit events that the toaster listens for and uses alternative placement. Eg: when overlay-depth > 0, place toasts top-right.

Omar: Good idea. I'll add event hooks. Also will surface in changelog so integrators know behavior changed.

Tess: I'll add visual tests for drawer + nested modal + toast interactions.

Rina: Thanks. Prioritize overlay-depth infra first. Toast listener can be follow-up.
